resources.string: Behaving properly next to parental controls
FamilyAware is an educational app that demonstrates correct behaviour on a device managed by parental controls, such as Google Family Link.
It only uses official Android APIs: it does not hide itself, does not change other apps\' settings, does not bypass restrictions and does not request privileged mechanisms.
The app needs exactly one runtime permission. Below is why it is needed and what happens if you refuse.
Refusing does not break the app: every screen and the whole diagnostic keep working, only sending notifications is disabled.
If a parent manages the device
FamilyAware inspects the device using official APIs and honestly reports when a feature is unavailable because of parental control.
In that case the app will not ask for the permission again. Instead it shows a clear message and step-by-step instructions on how a parent can officially allow the feature.
Needed to show the result of a check and to warn you when a feature is blocked by parental control.
If refused: the app keeps working but cannot show notifications. All other screens stay available.
On Android 12 and below this permission is granted at install time and is not requested at runtime — it is toggled in the app settings screen.

How a parent enables the mode

The app declares the boolean restriction persistentAccessAllowed. A device administrator, an MDM console or a parental control service sets it to true — and the mode turns on without any action from the app. Setting it to false forbids the mode, and the app obeys.

The \"Request the parent\'s approval\" button uses the official RestrictionsManager.createLocalApprovalIntent(): the request goes to the parental control service and the answer comes back to the app. Without a positive answer the mode is not enabled.
1. Open Family Link on the parent\'s device and select the child\'s profile.
3. Allow the app to run without a screen time limit — only a parent can do this.
4. If the app asks for approval — approve the request in the Family Link dialog.
What this mode does NOT do
Does not change system screen time limits and cannot change them — only a parent can, in Family Link.
Does not make the app a Device Owner or Profile Owner and does not use DevicePolicyManager.
Does not start a foreground service, wakelock or keep-alive to outlive restrictions.
Does not block uninstalling the app and does not disable its own components.
Does not hide the active mode: a persistent notification marker is always shown.
Does not override the administrator: persistentAccessAllowed = false always wins.
The mode only concerns this app. If a parent set a screen time limit, the system restricts the whole device regardless of this mode.
When enabled, the app runs in persistent access mode until the administrator revokes it. When disabled, the mode is unavailable and cannot be enabled on the device itself.

A separate mode for a device the parent officially allowed to use without screen time limits. Enabled only with a parent or administrator approval.
